$comment: Coverage gate config for @namzu/sdk. Consumed by .github/scripts/check-sdk-module-coverage.mjs and check-sdk-test-presence.mjs. The bucket rules were ratified in ses_006-test-coverage-sprint.
$comment_pricing: `pricing` is `required` with a measured floor, and the floor only means anything because its generated rate table is excluded from coverage in vitest.config.ts. Measured with the table IN: 299 lines, 282 of them the generated data, all counted covered the moment anything imports the module — so the aggregate read 100% while describing almost nothing, and the resolver could have lost a third of its lines and still cleared 97%. Measured with it OUT: 17 lines and 10 branches, all in index.ts, 100%/100%. Floor is measured minus 3 per the policy in check-sdk-module-coverage.mjs. Note the module is small enough that 3 points is less than one branch, so any uncovered branch in the resolver fails this gate — that is intended, not an accident of rounding.
$comment_coverageFloors: `runtime`, `store` and `manager` were the three critical modules with no floor; they are added here by issue #502. They were already `required`, so this is not a claim that they are untested -- `runtime` alone carries 192 test files, 187 of them under `runtime/query` -- it is the measurement that was missing, because test presence is not coverage -- a module can carry two hundred passing tests and still have whole failure paths that nothing executes. Measured on the parent commit, 718 files and 7355 tests, and unchanged on the commit that lands them (720 files and 7381 tests -- the two new test files and their 26 tests): `runtime` 91.18% lines / 89.69% branches, `store` 93.23% / 88.33%, `manager` 81.63% / 88.91%. Floors are measured minus 3 per the policy in check-sdk-module-coverage.mjs. `manager`'s floor of 78 is the lowest line floor of the three added here, because `manager` also has the lowest measured line coverage of the eleven (81.63% against `directory`'s 87.76). It is NOT the tightest floor relative to its own measurement, and keeping those two questions apart matters, because only the second one says whether a gate can still go red: against what they measured, the tightest floor in this file is `directory` (85 against 87.76, 2.76 points of slack), then `pricing` (3.00), `runtime` and `registry` (3.18, 3.19), `store` (3.23), `bridge` (3.49) and `manager` (3.63) -- while `connector`'s floor of 47 carries 47.48, making the lowest floor in this file also the loosest by an order of magnitude. `manager`'s floor sits at what that module actually holds; the next phase raises it by landing tests on the coordinators under `src/manager/` against their own failure paths -- `run/`, `resident/`, `project/`, and delegated agents under `manager/agent/`, where `lifecycle.ts` is what holds their budget -- rather than by raising the number. Two things to know before trusting any of these figures. The branch denominator is not run-stable: five coverage runs over the same `store` sources gave it four different branch denominators (3289, 3290, 3291, 3292) and a module aggregate ranging 88.32% to 88.36%, and between the last two of those runs 23 of the report's 486 rows moved in branch percentage, so a measured value carries a few hundredths of uncertainty, which is what the 3 points of slack absorbs. And a branch floor cannot see a module LOSE a path: deleting untested code takes its branch records with it and the ratio can go UP, so the line floor is set alongside the branch floor and not instead of it.
$comment_vitest4_remeasurement: RE-DERIVED 2026-09-18 from the vitest 4 measurement. Every floor above is floor(measured_v4 - 3): the policy this file has always stated, applied to a new instrument. No threshold was relaxed to make a run pass, and that is the sentence a reader six months from now needs in order to tell this apart from a quiet loosening -- the policy is unchanged, the calibration is new, and no floor moved because coverage was lost. It cannot have been lost: the two measurements differ ONLY in the vitest version. Same worktree, same config, same source tree, and the same 744 files and 7541 tests, all passing, in both runs. Vitest 4 replaced the v8 provider's remapping (`v8-to-istanbul` becomes `ast-v8-to-istanbul`), so the old numbers were never comparable to the new ones. The decisive evidence is one file, `src/utils/hash.ts`. Vitest 3 counted 20 lines in it and called 9 covered, 45%. Vitest 4 counts 7 and calls 1 covered. The file has 32 physical lines, 20 of them non-blank, and exactly 7 executable statements: 2 in `hashToolResult`, 4 in `buildToolResultHashes`, 1 in `stableDigest`. v4 is right. v3 was counting non-executable source lines as coverage units, and v4's lcov says so line by line -- `DA:28,2950`, `stableDigest`'s single line, executed 2950 times, against `DA:4,0`, `DA:5,0`, `DA:11,0`, `DA:12,0`, `DA:13,0`, `DA:15,0`, every line of the two functions that no test calls. The 13 extra lines v3 counted are filler that any executed file scores as covered the moment it loads, which is why the old percentages were INFLATED rather than merely different, and why the drop is a correction. The same effect package-wide, over an identical 548-file set: lines 66584 -> 26798, branches 23649 -> 21387, functions 3975 -> 5563, statements 66584 -> 30012, and as percentages lines 90.62 -> 89.43, branches 89.09 -> 83.62. Old floor -> new floor, with the v4 measurement each new floor comes from: advisory 94/91 -> 95/90 (98.3871/93.6416), bridge 96/95 -> 95/88 (98.8889/91.6049), bus 94/91 -> 93/87 (96.3115/90.8257), connector 47/84 -> 90/81 (93.7035/84.8321), directory 85/82 -> 86/80 (89.6996/83.8542), manager 78/85 -> 73/79 (76.2590/82.8094), pricing 97/97 -> 97/97 (100.0000/100.0000), rag 92/92 -> 92/89 (95.5923/92.6407), registry 93/90 -> 93/87 (96.5471/90.1454), runtime 88/86 -> 89/82 (92.5215/85.9372), store 90/85 -> 88/78 (91.9895/81.7416). TWO THINGS TO KNOW BEFORE TRUSTING THESE. (1) The re-derivation TIGHTENS four line floors, because some v3 floors had been set below measured - 3: advisory 94 -> 95, directory 85 -> 86, runtime 88 -> 89, and connector 47 -> 90 by a wide margin. connector's 47 was deliberate and this file used to say so -- it was named above as the lowest floor here and the loosest by an order of magnitude. Applying the policy uniformly erases that decision, so if the looseness was there for a reason, restore that one row by hand and record the reason; it is flagged here because a 43-point tightening is the only change in this commit that can go red on the NEXT edit rather than the last. (2) The apparent outlier did not survive checking. `manager` falls 5.80 points on the count-weighted aggregate this gate computes, four times any other module, which reads exactly like a module losing coverage. It is re-weighting, not loss: the same module's UNWEIGHTED mean of per-file line percentages falls only 1.79, and on that measure all eleven modules sit within 1.8 points of where they were, spread -1.79 to +0.18. v4 counts about 0.42 lines per line v3 counted and does so unevenly per file, so an aggregate that weights files by line count moves without any file's own percentage moving -- `src/manager/resident/learning.ts` goes 386 counted lines to 131 and stays at 100%, `src/manager/resident/store.ts` goes 203 to 61 and goes UP, 92.61 to 93.44. Branch deltas do NOT decompose as cleanly: unweighted they spread -7.49 to 0.00, because branch points are the unit the two remappers disagree about most -- v3 synthesised them from transpiled JavaScript, v4 derives them from the AST -- so these branch floors are a weaker ratchet in relative terms than the line floors, and should be watched rather than trusted to exactly 3 points. The slack analysis inside `$comment_coverageFloors` is a v3-measurement artefact and no longer describes these numbers; the table above is its replacement.
$comment_baseline_exempt: `baselineExempt` means ZERO-TESTED, per check-sdk-test-presence.mjs's own docblock. It had drifted badly: seven of its nine entries carried tests -- `utils` had 25 files -- so the list said 'these have no tests' about modules that did. A routing document that is false is worse than none, because the next person picks the wrong module to work on. Audited and corrected in ses_020, which left the two that genuinely had none. Both graduated to `required` in issue #502, in the commit that added their tests, so the list is empty and stays here as the bucket a new module lands in while it is dark -- empty is the state this file is supposed to be in, not one to refill. Measured on the commit BEFORE those tests landed: `model-router` 100% lines and branches, all 14 and all 8 of them, because `compaction.ts` calls `resolveTaskModel` on every compaction and `compaction-model-routing.test.ts` asserts every step of the chain from there -- covered, and covered from another module's tests, which is the gap the bucket was naming: nothing failed if the resolver was wrong for a task type compaction never asks about. `persona` measured 52.99% lines / 81.48% branches / 40% functions (62/117, 22/27, 2/5), every uncovered line in `persona/assembler.ts`, and every one of them a field a host sets: expertise domains, constraints, tool guidance, output discipline, and the whole of `mergePersonas` and `withSessionContext`. After their tests `persona` reads 117/117 lines, 58/58 branches, 5/5 functions. Neither carries a `coverageFloors` entry yet -- a floor for them is a separate ratchet, and these numbers are recorded here so it has something measured to ratchet from. Moving a module here into `required` asserts only that it HAS a test, which is what this gate checks -- coverage is the separate, opt-in `coverageFloors` claim.
